1  JUDGMENT 1. CHARGESHEET 1.1
As per the chargesheet, on 28.01.2011 SDM Kalkaji, District South, New Delhi recorded the statement of complainant Rakesh Singh at about 07.45 pm in his office.
1.2 Complainant stated that on 20.04.2006 he got married his daughter Supriya with Praveen Kumar Bhadoria and he had given the dowry articles in the said marriage as per his financial status.
At the time of marriage, there was no demand of any dowry from groom's side.
However, after her marriage, the in laws of her daughter started demanding dowry but he refused being financially incapable.
Thereupon, in laws of his daughter started torturing and harassing her.
His daughter told him that her mother in law Guddi Devi and her nanad Sapna used to beat her.
However, he did not complain the same to the police as he did not want to disturb his daughter's house.
On 26.01.2011 at about 07.00 pm he talked to his daughter Supriya on telephone and she told him that she was not well.
She felt like vomiting and giddiness.
She stated that they (her in-laws) were gettting her treated.

On this, he asked his daughter if she needs then he will come to her house but she stated that her treatment was going SC No. 1636/2016 State v. Praveen & Ors. Pages 2 of 31 on and he shall not hurry to come at her house.

His younger brother Anil, residing at Noida told him that Supriya was admitted in Metro Heart Institute, Sector 16, Faridabad and they directly reached at the said hospital where they came to know that their daughter had died.

The relevant legal provisions applicable in the present case are reproduced herewith:

Section 498A IPC provides "Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine."

Explanation:- For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
Section 304B provides "(1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonmentfor a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."

Section 113B Indian Evidence Act, 1872 provides "when the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman has been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death".

Further, the details of the dowry demands were not mentioned in either of said statements.
There is no independent witness regarding the allegations of dowry demand.

Moreover, the conduct of complainant and his brother do not correspond to their allegations of poisoning of deceased by her in laws.
Even the investigation of the case does not show that police made any efforts to check the veracity of the allegations.
Rather, the delay in filing the chargesheet against the accused persons show the lackadaisical attitude of the police.
The factum of marriage and the death SC No. 1636/2016 State v. Praveen & Ors. Pages 20 of 31 within seven years of marriage is not disputed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Explanation:- For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
Section 304B provides "(1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
Section 113B Indian Evidence Act, 1872 provides "when the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman has been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death".
SC No. 1636/2016 State v. Praveen & Ors. Pages 21 of 31 7.2
The key evidence against the accused is the alleged dying declaration of the deceased and the testimony of the complainant regarding the dowry demands and harassment of deceased due to non- fulfillment of such demands.
The dying declaration of the deceased has been sought to be proved through the complainant and his brother Anil Kumar.
However, the defence has disputed the alleged dying declaration and even the alleged dowry demands.
It is apparent that the fact that the daughter of complainant alleged or suspected that she has been poisoned by her in laws was too crucial to be omitted by the complainant when his statement was recorded by the SDM on 28.01.2011.
Rather it was the most important fact which should have been told by the complainant when he was examined by the SDM in regard to the circumstances of death of his daughter.
However, the conduct of PW3 as well as PW2 appear unnatural in case such allegations were made or even if such suspicion was expressed by the daughter of the complainant.
Moreover, in case the in laws of the deceased would have poisoned her forcefully or deceitfully, they would not have informed any family member of the deceased prior to her death.
However, no such person has been examined by the IO as to how he received such SC No. 1636/2016 State v. Praveen & Ors.
Had there been such serious allegations by the deceased, in all likelihood, PW3 Anil Kumar or other family members of deceased would have informed the police then and there.
Further, it has come in the cross examination of PW3 that deceased was taken to a private doctor on 26.01.2011.
In such case, if such allegations were made by the deceased, PW3 Anil Kumar SC No. 1636/2016 State v. Praveen & Ors.
Pages 25 of 31 or the other family members of the deceased would have taken the deceased to a qualified doctor under their own supervision instead of leaving the deceased with her in-laws.
Thus, from the aforesaid facts and circumstances,
the Court is convinced that no such dying declaration was made by the deceased in her conversation with her father.
Rather, the Court is put on caution to view the testimony of PW2 and PW3 with circumspection even regarding other allegations.
Secondly, there is no investigation regarding any CDR etc. to at least show that there used to be telephonic conversations between the deceased and the complainant.
Thirdly, PW2 has not specified the dates or even approximate timeline of harassment of deceased.
He has not even specified the date or the approximate timeline when he received such information from his daughter through phone.
Fourthly, he did not even state that he went to the house of her daughter or called for any meeting of any relatives or panchayat when he came to know about such harassment of the deceased.
However, he could not tell the date of this demand and only stated that this fact was also told to him by PW2.
However, his silence on the issue goes against the case of prosecution as he was the brother of complainant and would have been privy to such developments after the marriage of his niece.
8.3 In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in order to seek a conviction against a person for the offence of dowry death, the prosecution is obliged to prove that:-
a.The death of a woman was caused by burns or bodily injury or had occurred otherwise than under normal circumstance; b. such death should have occurred within seven years of her marriage;
c. the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or by any relative of her husband;
SC No. 1636/2016 State v. Praveen & Ors. Pages 30 of 31 d.such cruelty or harassment should be for in connection with the demand of dowry; and e. to such cruelty or harassment the deceased should have been subjected soon before her death.
However, the prosecution has failed to prove the requirements c, d and e illustrated in the said judgment.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Thus, from the facts of the case, defence of the accused, arguments of the parties and relevant provisions of law, the following points for determination arise:-
1. Whether the alleged dying declaration was made by the deceased?
2. Whether the prosecution has been able to prove the dowry demands and the harassment of deceased in relation thereof?
Whether the accused persons are liable to be convicted for any of the alleged offences?
